articles.title: Govt notifies grievance rules under VB-G RAM G Act, sets 15-day deadline
articles.summary: The Centre has notified rules for grievance redressal under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, mandating that complaints related to the implementation of the rural employment scheme be resolved within 15 days and providing for their escalation if they remain pending beyond the prescribed period. Under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026, notified by the Union Ministry of Rural Development, state governments will have to establish a three-tier mechanism at gram panchayat, block and district levels, the ministry said in a statement issued Monday. The rules provide for designated grievance redressal officers at each level to receive, register, enquire into and dispose of complaints. According to the ministry, grievances can be submitted in person, through speed post, a designated digital platform, telephone helplines or any other mode decided by state governments. articles.title: Jagan accuses SEC of complicity in civic poll malpractices, says YSRCP will go to court
articles.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:32 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy staging a protest outside the office of the Returning Officer in Pulivendula on Sunday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has accused the State Election Commission (SEC) of being complicit in the electoral malpractices that took place during the urban local body elections on November 1. Instead of protecting democracy, the SEC acted as per the whims of the coalition government, he said. In an X post on Monday, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said the shocking incidents during the municipal elections, particularly those in Pulivendula, exposed how the SEC stood firmly behind the malpractices. The State Election Commission (SEC), which is meant to protect democracy, has become subservient to @ncbn. The shocking incidents during yesterday's municipal polling across the state, including in Pulivendula, show how the SEC is enabling election irregularities. Yesterday in Pulivendula, YSRCP agents were kept out of 70 of the 80 polling booths. TDP goons brought in from other areas went on a rampage with the support of election officials and the police. They attacked our party agents to stop them from entering polling booths. In some places, they dragged our agents out of the polling stations. These incidents took place with the police's support. Voter slips were snatched from people, polling booths were captured, and votes were rigged and cast repeatedly. The video evidence of these incidents is clear. Agents from all 70 booths came to me personally, showed their agent forms to the officials, lodged complaints and protested. The entire state witnessed what happened. Yet the SEC's response was shocking. Irregularities took place in 70 of the 80 booths, and our agents were attacked and forced out. articles.title: ‘Modi, Shah & Nadda have lost sleep over opposition rally’s success,’ says Congress MP Manickam Tagore
articles.summary: Congress MP Manickam Tagore on Monday said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP president JP Nadda were rattled by the success of Sunday’s opposition rally, which called for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. “Modi, Shah and Nadda have lost sleep over the opposition rally’s success,” Tagore said, adding that the rally had sent a strong message that Gyanesh Kumar must go. He further said the opposition would decide its future course of action in the coming days.
